referee_caveats_inferred: The abstract cites 1D hydrodynamic models, but the text derives the planet mass from the DSHARP width-mass scaling, not a hydrodynamic run described here.
The planet mass range (4-70 MJup) spans the planet to brown dwarf regime and rests on assumed alpha, dust size distribution and h/r.
VLA 1b is a marginal detection (30 +/- 8 uJy, under 4 sigma) and its link to the CO hot spot is positional only.
Distance is never given as a number, so au conversions (gap width, radius, 49 au separation) cannot be checked.
The dust model is fit by eye with one wavelength and no uncertainties on the gap edges beyond ~5 au.

reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: One ALMA Band 6 project, 44 antennas, continuum plus 12CO/C18O cubes: likely tens of GB of raw data (inferred, not stated).
reproducibility.score_reason: The ALMA project code, band, beams, robust and rms are given, but calibration is deferred to an earlier paper, key imaging and self-calibration settings are missing, and the models are fit by eye; the main numbers (stellar mass, flux densities, mass ratios) are reported.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: The paper does not state that the data are public, self-calibration and imaging settings are incomplete, and the dust model is a by-eye fit that cannot be redone exactly.
